Dual-EEG hyperscanning / OpenNeuro ds007471

Two brains, one duet: no synchrony beyond the task

Sixteen pairs of people played short tone sequences together while both wore EEG caps. Their brain signals were no more synchronised with each other than with the same partner's signal from a different trial.

Preprocessed with MNE-Python, synchrony computed with HyPyP. Four measures, four frequency bands, a trial-shuffle control.

16
dyads analysed, 32 people
2,155
clean 2-second windows of joint playing
729
electrode links per map, 27 x 27
0 / 16
measure and band combinations where real partners beat shuffled partners
Method

From raw recording to a fair comparison

MNE-PYTHON
Clean

Linked-mastoid reference, 1 to 45 Hz band-pass, 250 Hz, ICA removal of eye movements, per person.

MNE-PYTHON
Cut

The first 8 s of every joint trial becomes four 2 s windows. Windows over 150 µV are dropped.

HYPYP
Couple

PLV, coherence, circular correlation and imaginary coherence between every electrode of one player and every electrode of the other.

CONTROL
Shuffle

Each window is re-paired with the partner's window from a different trial, same condition, same position. Repeated 20 times.

Both players hear the same tones and move at the same tempo, so their EEG looks alike even with no exchange between them. Shuffled pairs keep the task, the people and the electrodes and break only the shared moment. Real minus shuffled is what belongs to playing together.

Finding 1

Raw synchrony is well above zero, and so is the shuffled baseline

A theta-band PLV of 0.27 looks like coupling. The shuffled bars are the same height, because a 2 s window holds few slow cycles and phase locking by chance is high. A raw synchrony value says nothing by itself.

Finding 2

Real partners are within about 1% of shuffled partners

Per dyad, the difference scatters evenly around zero in every band and for every measure. All FDR-corrected q values are 0.97. Any whole-scalp partner-specific effect is smaller than roughly 2% of the baseline.

Finding 3

No electrode link stands out

None of the 729 links survives permutation correction in any of the 16 maps. The map below is the one that came closest (gamma coherence, corrected p = 0.058). Its one bright row is a single noisy electrode, CP5, not a network.

Finding 4

Duets and constant-pitch sequences do not differ reliably

Theta synchrony leans higher in musical duets for all four measures (imaginary coherence p = 0.08, uncorrected). Nothing survives correction. It is a lead for the full 32-dyad sample.

Reading the result

What it means

  • This is not evidence that inter-brain synchrony does not exist. In this task, with 2 s sensor-level windows, nothing remains once shared task structure is removed.
  • The baseline is strict on purpose. Comparing against rest or against strangers leaves shared stimulation inside the effect.
  • Half the dataset was used. The other usable dyads would tighten every interval.
Caveats

Choices to know about

  • The dataset README and the file headers disagree on which 32 channels are the left player. Headers were followed; inter-brain results do not depend on it.
  • sub-05 was left out (different channel layout). sub-13 kept only 43 windows.
  • Artifact rejection is a simple amplitude threshold, and ICA components were picked automatically.
  • Data: Zhou, Zamm, Christensen, Rao and Loehr, OpenNeuro ds007471 v1.0.0, CC0.
